title: Re-querying and proof size: Urquhart's conjecture and hole-faithful refutations
claim: (1) For bounded degree, Urquhart's conjecture (regular resolution polynomially simulates resolution on Tseitin formulas) on a family is equivalent to general resolution size 2^Omega(tw)/poly(n) on it; hence it holds on graphs with cell systems, bounded-degree minor-free graphs (planar included), linear-treewidth families and families with compact topological minors. (2) Read-2 branching programs of size 2m+2 compute satisfiable Tseitin formulas, so branching-program size arguments stop at regular resolution. (3) Hole-faithful refutations (no step forgets a variable touching the region where the hole must lie after the pivot is read) of a 2-edge-connected graph with an edge-linked set of w vertices have at least (1-4eps) 2^(eps w/2) clauses, so 2^Omega(tw): the hole of a random critical assignment stays uniform on the clause's region, regions fragment size-biased, and balanced regions are falsified with probability 2^-Omega(w). (4) Davis-Putnam refutations are regular and hole-faithful, so hole-faithful size is 2^Theta(tw) at bounded degree; a refutation of size 2^o(tw) must both re-read and forget at the hole's region. Urquhart's conjecture is not resolved.
failure_conditions: A carving or Davis-Putnam refutation on a checked instance is invalid, violates hole-faithfulness, lets a region grow along a walk, gives a non-uniform hole posterior given a walk prefix, or exceeds the 2^-fd passing bound.
The non-faithful control fails to make the hole posterior non-uniform on some declared instance.
A read-2 program errs on some assignment or reads a variable three times.
A published statement of the hole-faithful bound is found (novelty only).
foundation_claim_scope: Proof-complexity size bounds for Tseitin formulas; no contact-first claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py builds carving and Davis-Putnam refutations on seven graphs, verifies validity and hole-faithfulness, walks every critical assignment (exact hole posteriors per walk prefix and per node, monotone regions, passing fractions against (|K|/n) 2^-fd), runs a non-faithful control on four graphs, and verifies read-2 programs on all assignments; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with executable checks; cites Itsykson-Riazanov-Smirnov (2022) for the regular bound and the conjecture's status, Galesi-Talebanfard-Toran for the width version, Reed for well-linked sets, Ben-Sasson-Wigderson, and CELL-SIZE-20261020-001B-P001, GENERAL-SIZE-20261020-001B-P001; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: A targeted search on 2026-10-20 found Urquhart's conjecture listed as open (Itsykson-Riazanov-Smirnov 2022), the monotone cops-robber characterization of width, space and depth (Galesi-Talebanfard-Toran), and no lower bound for a class defined like hole-faithful refutations. The argument is Haken's counting method in Urquhart's probabilistic form; Theorem 1, Corollary 2 and Proposition 3 are short consequences of known results.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-20.
